# dtcloud_security_group (Resource)

Manages a security group -- the set of firewall rules applied to a machine's network interfaces.

The group is only a name and a description. The rules inside it are separate
`dtcloud_security_group_rule` resources, so adding or removing one rule leaves the group and every
other rule untouched.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "dtcloud_security_group" "web" {
  name        = "web-tier"
  description = "HTTPS from anywhere, SSH from the office"
}

# Rules are separate resources, so adding or removing one leaves the group and
# every other rule untouched.
resource "dtcloud_security_group_rule" "https" {
  security_group_id = dtcloud_security_group.web.id
  direction         = "ingress"
  protocol          = "tcp"
  port_range_min    = 443
  port_range_max    = 443
  remote_ip_prefix  = "0.0.0.0/0"
}
```

-> **Reference the group by `.id` from the machines that use it.** That tells Terraform the machine
depends on the group, so `terraform destroy` removes the machine first. A group written as a copied
id has no such dependency, and deleting it fails while something still uses it.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the security group. Can be changed in place. Names are not required to be unique.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Description of the security group. Can be changed in place, and removing it clears it.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `inbound_rule` (List of Object) Inbound rules as the platform displays them. Read-only; manage rules with dtcloud_security_group_rule. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--inbound_rule))
- `outbound_rule` (List of Object) Outbound rules as the platform displays them. A new group starts with two, added by the platform: allow-all IPv4 and IPv6 egress. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--outbound_rule))

## Behaviour worth knowing

* **Nothing here forces replacement.** Both arguments change in place, and removing `description`
  from the configuration clears it. That matters because the platform refuses to delete a group that
  is still in use, so a rebuild could never complete.
* **`inbound_rule` and `outbound_rule` are a display snapshot.** The details endpoint reports rules
  the way the web panel shows them: a protocol display name, the port range as text, and a referenced
  group by its name rather than its id. None of that can be turned back into a rule, which is why
  rules are their own resource and are read from a different endpoint. The snapshot is from this
  resource's last read, so rules created in the same apply appear after the next refresh.
* **A new group is not empty.** The platform adds two allow-all egress rules, one for IPv4 and one for
  IPv6. Terraform does not own them. To remove one, import it as a `dtcloud_security_group_rule`,
  then delete that resource from the configuration.
* **A group in use cannot be deleted.** The platform's refusal is passed through as it is. Destroy or
  detach whatever uses the group first.

## Timeouts

`create`, `update` and `delete` each default to 5 minutes. These calls are synchronous, so the
timeouts bound a hung request rather than a wait. Override them with a `timeouts` block:

```terraform
resource "dtcloud_security_group" "web" {
  # ...

  timeouts {
    create = "10m"
  }
}
```

## Import

```shell
terraform import dtcloud_security_group.web 7f9c1e40-1c3d-4b6a-9a2f-5f1c9d0e3b11
```

`name` and `description` are read back. The rules are not part of the import: each one is its own
`dtcloud_security_group_rule` and is imported separately, the two the platform created included.
